analysis.title: Global Macro Chart of the Day (#191): Sector contributions to the decline in global equity valuations
key_insights: Consensus expects S&P 500 earnings growth of 17.8% in 2027 and 16.9% in 2028. UBS flags a risk that forward earnings revisions start to roll over.
Historically the market has struggled when revisions to 12- and 24-month forward earnings growth turn negative, especially when starting expectations are as elevated as they are now.

This year began with 12-month forward growth expectations of 15.1%, against likely realised growth of 34.7%. Repeating that surprise depends heavily on the hyperscalers sustaining the AI infrastructure build-out.
Tech and Semis have derated sharply in the US and EM despite strong earnings. They account for nearly three-quarters of the market's derating.

UBS reads the derating as scepticism about the speed and size of the investment boom, and says it is not clear that company fundamentals have deteriorated. Cloud revenue growth was annualizing at about 100% in Q3, enterprise AI adoption is still low, and only part of the compute needed for future demand is in place.
UBS's end-2027 S&P 500 target is 8,900 and assumes no re-rating.

sector_views.rationale: UBS sees the sharp derating in US and EM Tech and Semis as a potential source of valuation support, since fundamentals do not appear to have deteriorated. It does not issue an explicit sector rating in this note.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 consensus earnings growth is 17.8% for 2027 and 16.9% for 2028 (consensus estimates, not reported).
12-month forward earnings growth expectations were 15.1% at the start of 2026, against likely realised growth of 34.7% (realised figure is UBS's estimate, not a final print).
Cloud revenue growth was annualizing at about 100% in Q3 (per UBS, reported basis not specified).
risk_factors: Forward earnings revisions for 12- and 24-month growth turn negative from elevated starting expectations.
The earnings outlook depends heavily on hyperscalers sustaining the AI infrastructure build-out.
Continued derating if investors stay sceptical about the sustainability of the investment boom.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech and Semis have derated sharply despite strong earnings, so valuations may support the market. Cloud revenue growth was annualizing at about 100% in Q3 and only part of the needed compute is in place. Earnings can surprise to the upside, as in 2026 when realised growth is likely 34.7% against 15.1% expected.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus already expects 17.8% growth in 2027 and 16.9% in 2028. The market has historically struggled when forward earnings revisions turn negative from elevated starting expectations, and the upside surprise depends on hyperscalers sustaining the AI build-out.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Revisions to 12- and 24-month forward earnings growth turning negative.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech and Semis derated sharply despite strong earnings, and it is not clear fundamentals have deteriorated, so valuations are becoming a potential source of support.
